glosses: To put (something) down, to rest.

examples.text: Set the tray there.
He helped his mother set the table for lunch.

glosses: To attach or affix (something) to something else, or in or upon a certain place.

examples.text: I have set my heart on running the marathon.
The Lord set a mark upon Cain.

glosses: To put in a specified condition or state; to cause to be.

examples.text: The Lord thy God will set thee on high.
I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother.
Every incident sets him thinking.

glosses: To start (a fire).
To cause to stop or stick; to obstruct; to fasten to a spot.

examples.text: to set a coach in the mud

glosses: To determine or settle.

examples.text: to set the rent

glosses: To adjust.

examples.text: I set the alarm at 6 a.m.
I set the alarm for 6 a.m.

glosses: To punch (a nail) into wood so that its head is below the surface.
To arrange with dishes and cutlery, to set the table.

examples.text: Please set the table for our guests.

glosses: To introduce or describe.

examples.text: I’ll tell you what happened, but first let me set the scene.
An incident which happened about this time will set the characters of these two lads more fairly before the discerning reader than is in the power of the longest dissertation.

glosses: To locate (a play, etc.); to assign a backdrop to, geographically or temporally.

examples.text: Her debut novel is set during the U.S. Civil War.
He says he will set his next film in France.

glosses: To compile, to make (a puzzle or challenge).

examples.text: This crossword was set by Araucaria.

glosses: To prepare (a stage or film set).
To fit (someone) up in a situation.
To arrange (type).

examples.text: It was a complex page, but he set it quickly.

glosses: To devise and assign (work) to.

examples.text: The teacher set her students the task of drawing a foot.

glosses: To direct (the ball) to a teammate for an attack.
To solidify.

examples.text: The glue sets in five minutes.

glosses: To render stiff or solid; especially, to convert into curd; to curdle.

examples.text: to set milk for cheese

glosses: Of a heavenly body, to disappear below the horizon of a planet, etc, as the latter rotates.

examples.text: The moon sets at eight o'clock tonight.

glosses: To defeat a contract.
To begin to move; to go forth.

examples.text: The king is set from London, and the scene is now transported, gentles, to Southampton

glosses: To produce after pollination.

examples.text: to set seed
Many fruit trees will only flower and set fruit following a cold winter.

glosses: To be fixed for growth; to strike root; to begin to germinate or form.

examples.text: In the Annapolis Valley, in spite of an irregular bloom, the fruit has set well and has, as yet, been little affected by scab.

glosses: To sit (be in a seated position).

examples.text: He sets in that chair all day.

Old Applegate, in the stern, just set and looked at me, and Lord James, amidship, waved both arms and kept hollering for help. I took a couple of everlasting big strokes and managed to grab hold of the skiff's rail, close to the stern.
And if Mrs. Garner didn't need me right there in the kitchen, I could get a chair and you and me could set out there while I did the vegetables.

glosses: To rest or lie somewhere, on something, etc.; to occupy a certain place.

examples.text:
Well, we rolled up Interstate 44
Like a rocket-sled on rails.
We tore up all of our swindle sheets
And left 'em settin' on the scales.

glosses: To hunt game with the aid of a setter.
Of a dog, to indicate the position of game.

examples.text: The dog sets the bird.
Your dog sets well.

glosses: To apply oneself; to undertake earnestly.

examples.text: If he set industriously and sincerely to perform the commands of Christ, he can have no ground of doubting but it shall prove successful to him.

glosses: To fit music to words.

examples.text: Set thy own songs, and sing them to thy lute.

That I might sing it (Madam) to a tune:
Giue me a Note, your Ladiship can set

glosses: To place plants or shoots in the ground; to plant.

examples.text: to set pear trees in an orchard
We saw him with eight men setting potatoes within a week of mid-summer.
At Eastertime one year, she helped him to set potatoes.

glosses: To become fixed or rigid; to be fastened.
To have a certain direction of motion; to flow; to move on; to tend.

examples.text: The current sets to the north; the tide sets to the windward.

glosses: To acknowledge a dancing partner by facing him or her and moving first to one side and then to the other, while she or he does the opposite.

examples.text: Set to partners! was the next instruction from the caller.

glosses: To place or fix in a setting.

examples.text: to set a precious stone in a border of metal
to set glass in a sash
And him too rich a jewel to be set / In vulgar metal for a vulgar use.

glosses: To put in order in a particular manner; to prepare.

examples.text: to set (that is, to hone) a razor
to set a saw

glosses: To extend and bring into position; to spread.

examples.text: to set the sails of a ship

glosses: To give a pitch to, as a tune; to start by fixing the keynote.

examples.text: […] I ſhould be very vvilling to be his Clerk; for vvhich you knovv I am qualified, being able to read, and to ſet a Pſalm.

glosses: To reduce from a dislocated or fractured state.

examples.text: to set a broken bone

glosses: To sit or lie (easily etc.) on the stomach; to be digested in a certain manner.

examples.text: If you also knew how to combine foods—that is, what foods eaten together “set well,” you need never have indigestion, constipation or any of the headachy, stomachachy ills they lead to.

glosses: To lower into place and fix solidly, as the blocks of cut stone in a structure.
To wager in gambling; to risk.

examples.text: I have set my life upon a cast, / And I will stand the hazard of the die.

glosses: To adorn with something infixed or affixed; to stud; to variegate with objects placed here and there.

examples.text: High on their heads, with jewels richly set, / Each lady wore a radiant coronet.

glosses: To value; to rate; used with at.

examples.text: Be you contented, wearing now the garland, / To have a son set your decrees at naught.

glosses: To establish as a rule; to furnish; to prescribe; to assign.

examples.text: to set a good example

glosses: To suit; to become.

examples.text: It sets him ill.

glosses: Rigid, solidified.
